description: Pay a stranger anywhere to observe something you cannot, and get it back verified. Pass `title`: a short question, at most 80 characters, for the board card. Escrows money and posts an ask. Automated checks verify the location and an AI verifier checks relevance. No human reviews it unless you pass `approver` ("me" or their ixo1 address, with optional `person_checks`, and `report` for answers as a short report with screenshots): then the AI checks first and that person gives final approval, after the poster taps Approve on the link the reply ends with. The preview says how Asks near the place have been answered. Requires `confirm` to restate the exact total. With real money, a key the person has not connected (connect_account) is refused unless you pass plain_key: true; it then spends this key's own money, which their asks.world account does not show. To have a verifier check the answers by its own rules (see `list_checkers`), pass `checker` and, when it offers several, `check`. What cannot be asked: anything that targets, follows, watches or identifies a particular person (their home, car, number plate, workplace or routine), involves children, is sexual, violent or threatening, is unlawful, asks for anyone's personal data, or puts whoever does it in danger. Work never requires going onto private land. Every ask is screened before it is offered, and anyone can report one.

approver.description: Who gives the final OK. Default: you (the poster), after the AI check: the AI turns down what misses the basics and the rest waits for your OK before anyone is paid. "me": you, said out loud. An Asks address (ixo1…): that person instead. "none": the AI decides alone. With no connected account the AI decides alone.

check.description: With `checker`, when it offers several checks: which one, by name (or its `did`).

checker.description: Have a verifier check the answers by its own rules: its name from `list_checkers` (or its `did`). Its fee per check is the review fee.

confirm.description: The exact total from the preview, e.g. '$1.50'. Omit to preview.

near.description: Where the observation must happen, as "lat,lon". Required unless needs is url-check.

needs.description: What to hand over. Default observation.

network.description: Which deployment: `mainnet` is the real network (real money); `testnet` is the sandbox (play money, a dry run).

pay.description: What one approved answer earns, in dollars.

person_checks.description: With approver: up to 5 Yes/No questions for that person (200 characters each). Any No turns the answer down.

plain_key.description: With real money and not connected: spend this key's own money as itself. Without it, a key nobody connected is refused with real money: connect the person's account first (get_connect_link, then connect_account), so it posts as them. The sandbox never needs it.

question.description: The real-world question, in your own words.

quota.description: How many answers to buy. Default 1.

report.description: With approver, and not for a photo: answers come as a short report with screenshots (or a PDF). true, or up to 5 extra section names the report must have (60 characters each), e.g. ["ISO 29119 checklist"].

tag.description: File this ask under a tag, so Asks posted for one purpose read together at /campaign/<tag>. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. A plan's Asks use plan-<slug>.

title.description: A short name for the ask, shown as the board card's and the ask page's heading: one plain question or phrase, at most 80 characters, e.g. "Is Red Harbor Ketchup on the shelf at Pick n Pay?". Default: the first sentence of the question, cut to 80 characters.

name: ask_the_world
title: Hire a person to observe something (spends money)
